items.label: Industry: Nuclear Power & Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) for AI Data Centers
items.detail: Selected via live-searched, news-prevalent theme rather than account holdings: the IBKR connector was not authenticated for this session (non-interactive run, OAuth unavailable), so this cycle could not be grounded in current account positions -- treat any overlap with existing holdings as unverified until the next run confirms it against live IBKR data. Nuclear/SMR power for AI data centers is one of the most consistently cited investment themes across September 2026 market outlooks: hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta) have collectively committed over 9.8 GW across 13 announced nuclear projects and more than $50B directly to nuclear power deals, the NRC finalized its first new reactor-licensing framework since 1989 ("Part 53", effective March 30, 2026), and a House vote on data-center power policy moved uranium/SMR stocks double digits in a single session on September 17, 2026 -- a genuinely live, fast-moving theme not covered by prior scout cycles (critical minerals 2026-08-31, GLP-1 2026-08-31, gaming 2026-09-06, search/ads/cloud 2026-09-13).

items.label: LEU
items.detail: Centrus Energy -- not confirmed held (IBKR unavailable this run). The clearest picks-and-shovels bottleneck play in the whole buildout: the US produces under 1% of global uranium-enrichment capacity, and Centrus is one of very few Western suppliers of HALEU (high-assay low-enriched uranium), the specific fuel most SMR/microreactor designs require. Centrus signed multiple new multi-year HALEU supply contracts in September 2026 (Antares Nuclear, Radiant) and completed a $500M capital raise to expand enrichment capacity; 18 covering analysts average a "Buy" rating with a 12-month price target of $253.25 against a last price of $144.90 (2026-09-19), a 47.9% implied upside. Real risk: revenue is still small relative to the capex Centrus needs to scale enrichment, it is heavily dependent on DOE-backed contracts and government cost-sharing, and its position as a US-strategic-supply chokepoint cuts both ways -- a political/funding disruption would hit it harder than a diversified industrial name.
items.suggested_size: Small starter satellite position, not core -- size formally against existing AI-infrastructure/uranium exposure once IBKR account access is restored.

items.label: CEG
items.detail: Constellation Energy -- not confirmed held (IBKR unavailable this run). The largest US nuclear-fleet operator and the counterparty on the highest-profile hyperscaler nuclear PPA to date (the Crane Clean Energy Center/Three Mile Island restart deal with Microsoft). Stock has pulled back roughly 25% from its October 2025 high of $413 to about $256 after 2026 EPS guidance of $11-12 missed consensus -- a real execution/guidance risk, not a manufactured dip, that has repriced even the "safest" incumbent nuclear-PPA name in the theme. Real risk: existing reactor fleet is a fixed, finite asset base (unlike SMR developers, Constellation cannot simply build more capacity quickly to capture incremental hyperscaler demand), and the guidance miss is a live signal that near-term earnings execution is not automatic even with structural demand tailwinds in place.
items.suggested_size: Modest position given the post-guidance-miss repricing already occurred; treat as a value entry into demand rather than a momentum add.

items.label: OKLO
items.detail: Oklo -- not confirmed held (IBKR unavailable this run). The purest direct-to-hyperscaler microreactor play: a 1.2 GW deal with Meta in southern Ohio, a $25M prepayment from Equinix for a future 20-year PPA covering up to 500 MW, and a total customer pipeline of 2,100 MW (+200% since its 2023 business-combination announcement). Stock jumped 13% to $40.37 on September 17, 2026 after a House vote on data-center power policy. Real risk: Oklo is pre-commercial-operation (no reactor generating revenue-producing power yet), and the same week's coverage explicitly flagged rising public/local backlash against data-center-linked nuclear siting as a real threat to both Oklo and NuScale -- this is a longer-duration, higher-variance bet than the incumbent-utility names above.
items.suggested_size: Small speculative starter position given pre-revenue/pre-commercial-operation status; size down relative to CEG/LEU.

items.label: CCJ
items.detail: Cameco -- not confirmed held (IBKR unavailable this run; prior scout cycles referenced CCJ as a critical-minerals holding, but that cannot be verified against live account data this run). The physical-commodity underpinning of the entire nuclear buildout: the uranium market faces an industry-wide 30-million-pound annual production shortfall against 70 GW of new global reactor capacity under construction, and Cameco has 230M lb under long-term contract with a 28M lb 2026 delivery target -- unusually high earnings visibility for a commodity producer. Real, current risk: the stock is down 7.23% over the past month, lagging both its own energy sector (+1.41%) and the S&P 500, because the McArthur River restart has proven more complex than initial guidance and Cigar Lake output has shown throughput variability -- a live reminder that even a structurally undersupplied commodity does not protect against single-operator execution risk.
items.suggested_size: Core-satellite sizing consistent with a structural commodity thesis; confirm against existing holdings once IBKR access is restored to avoid inadvertent doubling-up.

items.label: SMR
items.detail: NuScale Power -- not confirmed held (IBKR unavailable this run). A real strategic divergence from Oklo worth tracking rather than acting on yet: NuScale sells grid-scale SMR systems to utilities (its largest deal is a 6 GW system for the Tennessee Valley Authority) rather than contracting directly with hyperscalers the way Oklo does. Stock is down 36% YTD and trading near its $9.06 50-day moving average even as the broader nuclear/SMR theme has rallied on policy and demand headlines -- a genuine, unresolved question of whether the grid-scale go-to-market strategy is being penalized for slower near-term revenue visibility, or whether it will re-rate once TVA-scale units approach commercial operation. Carry forward to the next scout cycle to see which strategy the market rewards first.

items.label: Nuclear siting & local-opposition risk
items.detail: No specific ticker, theme-level risk signal: multiple September 2026 pieces (including coverage explicitly naming Oklo and NuScale) flag rising public backlash against data-center-linked nuclear/SMR siting -- water use, environmental review, and community opposition that can stall a project even after federal NRC approval. This is a genuine execution risk sitting underneath every name in this cycle's opportunity set, not a hypothetical: state and local siting fights operate on a different, less predictable timeline than the federal licensing reforms driving the bullish case. Worth tracking project-by-project rather than pricing in as a blanket discount.

items.label: NRC Part 53 licensing reform
items.detail: No specific ticker, theme-level regulatory tailwind with an offsetting risk: the NRC's final rule on a new reactor licensing process ("Part 53", effective March 30, 2026) is the first new US reactor-licensing framework since 1989, explicitly designed to make advanced-reactor licensing faster, simpler, and more cost-effective, and NRC officials have credited AI tools with cutting licensing review times. The same reform has drawn criticism from some who argue the NRC is moving too fast and jeopardizing safety review rigor -- a live governance/safety debate that could slow or reverse the pace of approvals this whole theme currently assumes. Track for any signs of a safety incident or political reversal that would undercut the licensing-speed thesis.
